name: Enterprise Stakeholder Interest and Engagement
constraints: WM-ORG-013 masters a context-specific party-to-subject Stakeholder Interest relation without remastering party identity.

Each WM-ORG-013 stakeholder relation has an addressable perimeter-qualified bitemporal instance key so assessments, expectations, plans and challenges can cite the relation rather than the party master.
Expectation is an attributed WM-KNW-007 claim bound to the stakeholder relation.
Stakeholder Assessment profiles WM-ACT-034 with the stakeholder relation rather than the party as its subject.
Engagement Plan profiles WM-ACT-008 while execution and outreach remain separate acts.
Every role, interest, expectation, influence, impact or approach binds subject matter, perimeter, viewpoint, validity, knowledge time and evidence or explicit unknown.
Client, owner, executor and stakeholder are independent roles and none implies another.

Declared interests are WM-ORG-013 relation content; analyst hypotheses or imputed interests are attributed, contestable WM-KNW-007 claims and never write to the relation or party master; contradictory interests may coexist.
Missing, withheld and not-yet-heard are distinct from no interest or consent.
Influence, impact and priority are dated assessments with pinned method, scale, evidence, assessor, uncertainty and re-assessment triggers.

Reassessment creates a successor WM-ACT-034 record that cites and preserves the immutable prior record; the successor carries its own dated method, uncertainty, evidence and assessor, and any reuse is an explicit re-derivation rather than inheritance.
Indeterminate is distinct from low and an assessment never generalizes across perimeter, viewpoint or period.
Stakeholder registration grants no outreach, disclosure or decision authority.
Execution-adjacent use requires a pinned external permission or decision authority reference; absent authority is recorded as explicit unknown and fails closed.
Representation mandates are scoped and contestable; dissent and minority positions remain attributable.
Conflict-of-interest handling records declaration, independent determination, recusal and recalculation of affected thresholds.
Sensitive interests, affiliations and personality traits cannot be inferred and exports retain scope, record-level restrictions and loss warnings.
Projection, aggregation and cross-perimeter copy preserve privacy restrictions, representation scope and attributable dissent; hidden evidence cannot be reconstructed from a published rating.

Cross-perimeter rollup or party-level joining of ratings is prohibited; any authorized multi-perimeter publication requires explicit inference review and remains a projection rather than a party attribute.
Restricted claims and evidence are redacted with non-reconstructive presence markers that preserve missing, withheld, not-yet-heard, indeterminate and low as distinct states.
Deletion of a record never extinguishes an underlying right, impact or grievance.
holds: All bases remain non-canonical reviewable drafts.
WM-ORG-013 has a registry parent/reference conflict and no ratified relation rows.
The v1 bare influence code must be retired in favor of assessment semantics.
WM-ACT-034 access claims and WM-KNW-010 conflict-of-interest structures remain weak.
The external permission/decision authority type must be pinned before execution-adjacent use; explicit unknown remains deny-by-default.
The single frozen audit was remediated without a repeat; canonical publication authority was not granted.
